findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

Over 13 gnats were observed in the storage hallway off of the kitchen. They appeared to be focused around the raw onions and investigation showed a couple of the onions were rotten. The PIC was shown and the onions discarded during the inspection. A follow up is being set for 10 days to ensure that the flies are removed from the facility. The PIC was instructed to use their pest control to ensure that this happens. Ensure that the facility is maintained free of pests at all times.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

The CFPM available during the inspection did not have a completed allergen training certificate available during this inspection. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to ensure that all CFPMs have a completed allergen training certificates at all times. Complete the training and certification prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

On arrival the facility could not produce their reporting agreements (from a previous inspection) or similar paperwork. Fresh copies of the Sangamon County Reporting Agreements were given to the facility and signed during the inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that all needed paperwork is available at all times in the facility.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.citation_text:
3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD (RTE) with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

An employee was observed chopping lettuce that was intended for use in salads while using their bare hands to hold it. Education was conducted and gloves donned to correct. Ensure that all RTE foods are not handled with bare hands throughout the preparation process.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11(C) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (C) Except as specified in (D) of this section, if used with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD, EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be cleaned throughout the day at least every 4 hours.

The blade of the can opener in the kitchen was observed soiled during the inspection. An employee stated that the can opener had not been used yet today, indicating that the blade was soiled prior and not correctly cleaned at the end of the day. The employee moved the item to dish for immediate cleaning to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces of equipment are cleaned regularly and at least every 4 hours.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

The insides of the standing freezer as well as the chest freezer in the back area were observed soiled with chicken juice. The equipment also has significant frost accumulation. The PIC is instructed to clean these locations and maintain them clean at all times moving forward.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11(C) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (C) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be kept in the original protective PACKAGE or stored by using other means that afford protection from contamination until used.

Multiple cup holders in the kitchen are used for storing plastic utensils. These containers are observed soiled at the time of this inspection. The PIC was shown and moved the holders to dish for cleaning. The plastic utensils were discarded as well. Ensure that all single service items are stored so that they are protected from contamination at all times.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.11(B) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (B) EQUIPMENT components such as doors, seals, hinges, fasteners, and kick plates shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted in accordance with manufacturer's specifications. 

Duck tape is being used to hold the central pole of the door frame together of the standing cooler across from the dish machine in the kitchen. The situation was discussed with the PIC. This equipment needs to be repaired correctly and the use of duck tape should cease in relation to the food equipment and food contact surfaces in the facility.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

On arrival sani bucket were not prepared in the facility. Once employees noticed the inspector’s arrival they went and prepared the two normal sani buckets in the kitchen. Significant food preparation and handling were observed to have taken place prior to the inspector’s arrival. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they were made aware that they sani buckets should be ready for use at any time that foods are being handled.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(3) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (3) Nonabsorbent for areas subject to moisture.

The hand sink in the women’s bathroom is observed with gaps forming at the wall/sink junctions. The PIC is instructed to re-seal these locations so that a smooth and easily cleanable surface is present at all times. Ensure smooth and easily cleanable surfaces at all times around the water sources in the facility.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.citation_text:
3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

An employee was observed to sprinkle chopped nuts onto sauce with their bare hands. Education was conducted and the items discarded to correct. Ensure that ready to eat (RTE) foods are protected from contamination by the use of gloves or utensils while handling.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11(C) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (C) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be kept in the original protective PACKAGE or stored by using other means that afford protection from contamination until used.

1) Multiple cup holders in the kitchen are used for storing plastic utensils. These containers are observed soiled at the time of this inspection. The PIC was shown and moved the holders to dish for cleaning. The plastic utensils were discarded as well. 2) A pen and a sharpie are observed in a container along with Dixie cups/lids. Pens and sharpies are not cleaned/sanitized and are not generally considered clean for the purposes of food contact. The PIC was shown and moved the implements to the pen cup observed a foot away and discarded the Dixie cups to correct. Ensure that all single service items are stored so that they are protected from contamination at all times.

findings.citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(3) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (3) Nonabsorbent for areas subject to moisture.

The hand sinks in the women’s bathroom and the employee bathroom in the back are observed with gaps forming at the wall/sink junctions. The PIC is instructed to re-seal these locations so that a smooth and easily cleanable surface is present at all times.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.citation_text:
6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

A pair of personal drinks (opened) are observed stored on the top shelf over multiple shelves of plates. The PIC was shown and told to place in use personal drinks under and/or away from food contact surfaces in the kitchen. The drinks were moved during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. 

Multiple flies are observed in the back storage room and several more in the men’s bathroom during this inspection. Flies appear to be of the fruit/drain variety and approximately eight are observed total. The PIC is instructed to remove the pest concern prior to the follow up in 10 days.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

The inner shelf of the chest freezer in the back room is being held together with metallic tape. The tape appears to be clean at this time but a crack is currently exposed with this method of temporary repair. Repair/replace to ensure a smooth and easily cleanable surface.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

A cup of water is observed on a counter next to foods being used to prepare for service. Education was conducted and the cup removed to correct. Ensure that personal drinks are stored and consumed away from foods intended for consumers.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. 

On arrival, a large bowl and a pitcher are observed in the hand sink to the left of the three part sink, blocking it. The items were removed during the inspection to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are maintained available for easy use at all times.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.13: (A) floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1mm (one thirty-second inch). 

The wall/floor junction in the employee bathroom is observed with a gap of approximately an inch along the wall next to the toilet. This location does not appear to be getting sufficiently cleaned. Clean the location and extend the baseboard/coving around the wall to cover this area

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

1) The wire shelves across from the woks have significant oil/grease accumulation. 2) The air vents in front of the hood system have significant oil/grease build up taking place. Ensure sufficient cleaning is taking place to keep these areas, and the facility in general, clean.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

1) The inner shelf of the chest freezer in the back room is being held together with strips of duck tape. The tape appears to be clean at this time but is unlikely to be able to be maintained this way. A crack is also left with this method of temporary repair. Repair the lid correctly so that it is smooth and easily cleanable. 2) Shelves in the standing freezer in the back storage room are held together with metallic tape. One of the shelves has broken the tape and allows for a large crack/gap. Repair/replace to ensure a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
